findings.title: Queries that interpolate to an empty expr are no longer dropped, which can leave the shard observable hanging
findings.body:
The old code interpolated first and then ran `.filter((query) => query.expr)`. The new code filters on the raw `expr` and only then calls `applyTemplateVariables`. A query such as `expr: '$var'` whose variable resolves to an empty string now passes the filter and comes out with `expr: ''`.

What happens next:
- `groupTargetsByQueryType` puts it in the `otherQueries` group, because `requestSupportsSharding` rejects empty exprs.
- `runNextRequest` calls `runSplitQuery` with that group. `runSplitQuery` filters out empty exprs, so `requests` is `[]`.
- `runSplitGroupedQueries` then throws synchronously at `requests.filter(...)[0].partition` (querySplitting.ts line 96).
- The throw happens inside the `.then()` of `groupTargetsByQueryType`, so it becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The subscriber is never completed or errored, and the panel stays in loading state forever.

This triggers when the request has a shardable query plus a non-shardable query whose variable is empty. Fix: filter `query.expr` after interpolation, here and in `runSplitQuery`, as the previous implementation did.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables (including ad-hoc filters) now runs multiple times per query
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`. Each sub-request then goes through `datasource.runQuery` → `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, which calls `applyTemplateVariables` again with the same `request.filters`. In the shard path, `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates as well, so each query is processed three times.

Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent: it calls `addAdHocFilters`, which appends ad-hoc filters to the expression. Stream-selector placement de-duplicates via `labelExists`. For queries with a parser (e.g. `{app="x"} | json`), filters go through `addFilterAsLabelFilter`, which has no dedup. The result is queries like `| level=`error` | level=`error` | level=`error`` sent to Loki and shown in the inspector.

Variable values containing `$name` text, and ad-hoc filter values, are also re-interpolated on each pass. The previous shard code deliberately used `interpolateVariablesInQueries` without filters, leaving ad-hoc filter application to the backend-query step.

The updated test asserting `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times codifies this redundant processing. Consider interpolating only variables (no `filters`) here, or marking targets as already interpolated so later passes skip ad-hoc injection.

findings.title: New interpolation test relies on a mock that interpolates `$__auto`, which the real code never does
findings.body:
The test's `replace` mock replaces `$__auto` unconditionally and ignores the scopedVars passed in. The real `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` explicitly strips `__auto`, `__interval`, `__range`, etc. from scopedVars so they pass through to the backend. In production, `$__auto` therefore stays uninterpolated at this stage.

The test asserts behaviour that cannot happen with the real template service. It also does not check what the change is supposed to fix: that splitting decisions (log vs. metric partitioning, `calculateStep` grouping by `step`) are made on interpolated values.

The same pattern is copied into `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`. Use a regular dashboard variable and assert on the grouping or partition outcome instead.
